context:
You asked, 14:45 CDT: did I build this right? You saw no picture in the card, only View. No, it wasn't right on your screen: those pictures draw by a script, and the live page most likely doesn't run a picture's script inside a card (unproven; in my headless check it drew). Now each option shows a still picture, which needs no script.

Some option pictures zoom to one part of a mockup. When that part is taller than the card's 480px picture box, the picture now scrolls. #806 ships 1A; 1B is the other way. Not blocking: #806 merges either way.

options.gain: The picture keeps showing what the option is about; matches the page rule that a zoomed picture shows that part whole.
options.how: As built in #806: the scroll stays inside the zoomed part and opens at its top.
options.label: 1A: only the zoomed part scrolls
options.lose: You can't scroll out to see the rest of the screen from the card; View shows it.

options.gain: The rest of the screen is one scroll away, right in the card.
options.how: The card opens at the zoomed part but lets you scroll the whole mockup.
options.label: 1B: the whole mockup scrolls
options.lose: Easy to scroll off the part that matters; the page rule changes.

ref: c204 (a tall picture on a waiting-page card scrolls), PR #806, batch 21; mockup docs/design/c204-scroll.html on its branch
title: When a card's picture zooms to one part, what scrolls?
why: The builder, reviewers and designer all chose 1A; it keeps each card about one thing.
